papers.title_in_file: Quantum algorithms to simulate quadratic classical Hamiltonians and optimal control
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, statements of Theorems 7 and 8, conclusions; proofs in Sections 4 and 5 not read.
papers.what_it_is: Riverlane paper giving quantum algorithms for damped coupled oscillators and Riccati equations, with a BQP hardness result.

assertions.value: The paper proves that estimating the kinetic energy of a damped coupled oscillator system to within additive precision is BQP hard when the damping strength is bounded by an inverse polynomial in the number of qubits.
quotes: We show that estimating the kinetic energy at a given time of this system to within additive precision is BQP hard when the strength of the damping term is bounded by an inverse polynomial in the number of qubits.
This means that unless BPP = BQP, no classical algorithm can solve this problem efficiently.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 8, Section 4; stated in abstract and Section 6
assertions.reader_inference: The classical-hardness statement rests on the BPP = BQP assumption.

assertions.value: The authors state that, to their knowledge, theirs is the first example of a nonlinear differential equation solved when the strength of the nonlinearity is asymptotically greater than the amount of dissipation.
quotes: To our knowledge, this is the first example of any nonlinear differential equation that can be solved when the strength of the nonlinearity is asymptotically greater than the amount of dissipation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Priority claim by the author, hedged with 'to our knowledge'.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum algorithm is efficient for damping strengths that are polylog(d) in the dimension d, but the hardness result requires a strength below some inverse polynomial, so the two regimes do not match.
quotes: the quantum algorithm for damped coupled oscillators is efficient for damping strengths that are polylog(d), where d is the dimension.
However, the hardness result requires that the strength be less than some inverse polynomial.
assertions.certainty_reason: Open problems list, Section 6

papers.title_in_file: Eliminating Vendor Lock-In in Quantum Machine Learning via Framework-Agnostic Neural Networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, hardware validation setup, discussion, conclusion; benchmark tables only skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: Academic paper presenting a framework-agnostic quantum neural network architecture with a hardware abstraction layer, benchmarked on three datasets and on IBM and other QPUs.

assertions.value: The authors report training time within 8% overhead of native framework implementations with identical classification accuracy on Iris, Wine and MNIST-4, and a maximum accuracy difference of 0.3 percentage points.
quotes: demonstrating training time parity (within 8% overhead) compared to native framework implementations, while achieving identical classification accuracy
the maximum accuracy difference is 0.3 percentage points
assertions.certainty_reason: Own benchmark on three small datasets, simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: The words identical accuracy and a 0.3 point maximum difference are not the same statement.

assertions.value: The authors report that on IBM Brisbane the QPU and simulator parameter-shift gradients agreed for three of four parameters, and state this is consistent with noise margins.
quotes: Hardware validation on IBM Brisbane (127 superconducting qubits) confirms that parameter-shift gradients computed through the HAL agree with simulator predictions within noise margins.
The agreement between QPU and simulator gradients for three of four parameters
assertions.certainty_reason: Single 2-qubit experiment, Table 7.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract wording is stronger than the one parameter that disagreed.

assertions.value: The authors state, in the note to the cross-vendor table, that the IQM Garnet results are pending a device calibration window.
quotes: IQM Garnet tasks submitted via AWS Braket; results pending device calibration window.
assertions.certainty_reason: Table 10 note, p.21
assertions.reader_inference: The conclusion nevertheless lists IQM among four backends with gradient error results.

quotes: Our approach leverages automatic differentiation of the energy functional to obtain nuclear gradients at a computational cost comparable to that of energy evaluation.

assertions.value: The authors report that training ML models with only energy data gave large errors in gradient predictions, and that the advantage of adding gradient training data grew with system size.
quotes: It was also found that training ML models with just energy data resulted in large errors in gradient predictions, and the relative advantage of including gradient training data

assertions.value: The authors state that automatic differentiation through stochastic reconfiguration yields biased gradients and that reverse-mode differentiation carries a large memory overhead.

papers.title_in_file: WSBD: Freezing-Based Optimizer for Quantum Neural Networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, experiment overview, noisy-simulation discussion, conclusion, appendix proof scope statement.
papers.what_it_is: AISTATS 2026 paper proposing a parameter-freezing optimizer for QNN training, evaluated by simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that WSBD converges on average 63.9% faster than Adam for the ground-state-energy problem, with an advantage that grows with QNN size.
quotes: Our extensive evaluation shows that WSBD converges on average 63.9% faster than Adam for the popular ground-state-energy problem, an advantage that grows with QNN size.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation study by the optimizer's authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that their convergence proof is tailored to the standard gradient descent update rule and so guarantees convergence for the WSBD-SGD variant only; the Adam case is left to future work.
quotes: This proof of convergence is specifically tailored to the standard gradient descent update rule, thereby formally guaranteeing convergence for the WSBD-SGD variant.
a formal convergence proof for adaptive optimizers like Adam is considerably more complex
assertions.certainty_reason: Appendix A, proof scope paragraph
assertions.reader_inference: Part of the abstract's convergence proof claim covers only the SGD variant.

assertions.value: The authors report that, under simulated IBM Heron-calibrated noise, WSBD-SGD required 58% fewer forward passes than SGD and WSBD-Adam reduced forward passes by more than 80% on a small VQE problem.
quotes: we simulate errors calibrated from IBM Heron devices
WSBD-SGD required 58% fewer forward passes than SGD, while WSBD-Adam reduced forward passes by more than 80%
assertions.certainty_reason: Noise simulated, not run on hardware.

papers.title_in_file: Beyond the Expressivity-Trainability Paradox: A Dynamical Lie Algebra Perspective on Navigating Barren Plateaus in Quantum Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Whole text read except the reference list.
papers.what_it_is: Short theory-plus-simulation paper linking dynamical Lie algebra dimension to barren plateaus, with a symmetry-preserving ansatz tested on a two-moons task.

assertions.value: The authors state that they verified that restricting the dynamical Lie algebra to polynomial growth is a necessary algebraic condition to prevent exponential gradient vanishing.
quotes: We verified that restricting the DLA to a polynomial growth rate is a necessary algebraic condition to prevent exponential gradient vanishing.
assertions.certainty_reason: Conclusion statement; text describes it as a synthesis of prior DLA results and an empirical link.
assertions.reader_inference: The word necessary is stronger than the empirical link the authors describe.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the Make Moons task at n = 8 the hardware-efficient ansatz (30 layers, over 700 parameters) reached nearly 100% accuracy, while the symmetry-preserving ansatz plateaued at around 83.5%.
quotes: At n = 8, the system size is on the threshold before the absolute onset of Barren Plateaus.
the highly expressive HEA (configured with 30 layers and over 700 parameters) successfully minimizes the loss, achieving a classification accuracy of nearly 100%
resulting in a plateaued but robust accuracy (around 83.5%)
assertions.certainty_reason: One small simulated task.

assertions.value: The authors state that whether geometric constraints give resilience against noise-induced barren plateaus remains an open question.
quotes: whether geometric constraints offer inherent resilience against noiseinduced barren plateaus
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 5 future work

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Algorithms for Unsupervised Machine Learning and Neural Networks (PhD thesis, Jonas Landman)
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Ch. 5 dequantization discussion, Ch. 8 and 9 conclusions, Ch. 12 conclusion, thesis conclusion; proofs and most chapters not read.
papers.what_it_is: PhD thesis with quantum algorithms for k-means, spectral clustering, convolutional and orthogonal neural networks, with simulations.

assertions.value: The author states that the thesis proves the quantum algorithms are faster than their classical versions but show random effects due to the quantum computation.
quotes: We prove that these quantum algorithms are faster compared to their classical version, but exhibit random effects due to the quantum nature of the computation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract claim; proofs not read by this reader.
assertions.reader_inference: Speed-ups assume fault-tolerant hardware and quantum data access, as the abstract itself says.

assertions.value: The author states that the running times should be interpreted with subtlety because they depend on parameters that often depend on the data values themselves.
quotes: These running times should be interpreted with subtlety as they depend on counter intuitive parameters, that often depends on the data values themselves.
assertions.certainty_reason: Thesis conclusion, p.175

assertions.value: The author reports that simulations show the delta-k-means convergence is almost the same as regular k-means for large enough delta, which the thesis takes as evidence for q-means accuracy.
quotes: In conclusion, our simulations show that the convergence of
provides evidence that the q-means algorithm will have as good performance as the classical k-means
assertions.certainty_reason: Classical simulation of the noise model, not a quantum run.

assertions.value: The author states that it remains an open question to find classical algorithms for these machine learning problems that are polylogarithmic in the dimension and competitive with the quantum ones.
quotes: It remains an open question to find classical algorithms for these machine learning problems that are polylogarithmic in the dimension and are competitive with respect to the quantum or the classical algorithms for the same problems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's survey of the field state.
